rationale: Create clear channels for security incidents and concerns. Private vulnerability disclosure is related but does not cover internal incident and concern reporting. Keep both channels and their audiences explicit.
Provide anonymity for security reporters. A private channel is not necessarily anonymous; specify anonymity capability and limits rather than asserting it from privacy.
Review and improve communication processes regularly. Reachability of a disclosure channel alone does not establish recurring process review and improvement.
Promote security awareness and responsibility throughout the organization. Training completion alone does not establish the organizational culture and accountability objective.

Encourage open discussions about security. Engineering feedback channels support discussion but do not by themselves establish open security dialogue; protect sensitive information while retaining the recommendation.
Integrate security into all aspects of the development lifecycle. Education is supporting evidence, not proof of lifecycle-wide security integration.

Ensure Enterprise configuration follows security and compliance best practices. Assessment is necessary evidence but does not itself establish conforming configuration; define the applicable baseline and retain unmet items.

Name responsible Enterprise configuration individuals and establish regular communication with Support, Services and Partners. Generic authority assignment does not establish these named owners and coordination relationships.
Review Enterprise settings regularly and update them as needed. Versioned change control does not establish recurring review of existing settings.
Document Enterprise configuration changes and approvals. The canonical approval and rollback trace supports this, but target Enterprise configuration and actual approval records need explicit scope.
Implement Enterprise SSO. The source recommends actual implementation; the local authentication profile can choose supported architecture, but evaluation alone cannot discharge this recommendation.
Ensure secure SSO configuration and review it regularly. Authentication-policy verification alone does not establish secure settings and recurring review.
Train users in SSO usage and its benefits. Secure-development training does not establish authentication training or the benefits component.

Establish and regularly test Enterprise backup and recovery procedures under the explicit Enterprise Server heading. Preserve both procedure establishment and recurring tests; generic recovery testing lacks recurrence.
Store Enterprise Server backups securely. An isolated restoration test does not establish secure backup storage and associated access protection.
Document Enterprise Server backup and recovery processes. Preserve backup as well as restoration procedures; generic tested recovery does not establish documentation.
Test backups and actual restores into staging regularly. The canonical isolated restore test supports the objective, but recurring testing and both backup and restoration must remain visible.

Implement network safeguards protecting Enterprise instances, with VPNs and firewalls as examples. Select deployment-appropriate measures through explicit target policy; do not assume Cloud and Server have identical control surfaces.
Review and update network-security configurations regularly. Generic maintained settings do not establish a scheduled review and actual change evidence.
Monitor network traffic for suspicious activity. Preserve traffic-monitoring coverage and detected activity evidence, without asserting that every packet must be retained.

Automate provisioning and deprovisioning for timely access management; SCIM is an example. Identity reconciliation alone does not establish automation and timeliness; feature limits require explicit treatment.
Review user access and permissions regularly. The canonical periodic review supports this but must preserve Enterprise target scope and user access as well as individual grants.
Implement 2FA for all users. Applicable authentication-policy verification cannot silently replace all-user coverage; platform and identity-provider distinctions require an explicit target decision.
Develop and enforce security policies specific to the Enterprise environment. General governance training does not prove deployment-specific policy enforcement.
Review and update Enterprise security policies regularly. Keeping policy current is not evidence of the recurring review and update process.
Communicate Enterprise security policy to all relevant stakeholders. Training governance policies does not demonstrate communication coverage for this deployment.
Secure Enterprise APIs with appropriate authentication and authorization. Preserve both access controls and the API target, rather than assuming repository permission reviews cover API mechanisms.
Monitor API use for anomalies. Investigating anomalies after discovery does not establish the upstream monitoring objective.

Establish API-use best-practice guidelines, including token use. Short-lived workflow credentials are narrower than guidelines for all Enterprise API use; preserve token handling and permitted API practices.
Establish monitoring and alerts for unusual Enterprise activities. Service-alert rules do not cover every Enterprise administrative or security event; retain broader Enterprise activity scope.
Review and update monitoring rules and audit logs regularly. Audit retention alone does not establish recurring rule review, configuration maintenance or log examination.
Ensure Enterprise security alerts are actionable and promptly addressed. Routing alerts to owners does not demonstrate actual prompt treatment; define response expectations without inventing an SLA.
Meet applicable data-residency requirements, especially for Enterprise Server replication. Identifying obligations and qualified review alone do not establish conformity or replicated-data coverage.
Review data-residency configurations regularly. Obligation identification is related but does not establish a recurring configuration review.
Document data-residency policies and procedures. Qualified review does not establish both maintained policy and procedural documentation.
Review and secure Enterprise third-party integrations to prevent security risk. Installation inventory and permission review do not establish actual securing of the integration.
Assess third-party integration security regularly. A one-time inventory and revocation path do not establish recurring security assessment.
Ensure third-party providers conform to the organization's security standards. Checking a provider is evidence gathering, not the conformity outcome itself.
Assess repository organization and structure for clarity and scalability. Function ownership supports this but does not establish assessment of growth and comprehensibility in Enterprise deployment.
Determine naming-convention use and ensure every repository has a description. Preserve the different modalities: naming is assessed, descriptions are required by the recommendation.

Check use of custom properties to organize repositories and target rulesets. This is a specific capability-assessment recommendation; do not infer required adoption or platform availability from the frozen link.

Verify appropriate repository segmentation, avoiding unnecessary monoliths while determining when monolithic architecture is necessary. Preserve both the segmentation and justified-monolith alternative; polyrepo default cannot erase it.
Check branch-protection use for code quality. Effective-rule inspection is relevant, but this source does not itself prescribe particular review thresholds, checks or bypass policies.
Evaluate code modularity for maintainability and scalability. A preference for reusable components does not establish the assessment or its two outcomes.
Ensure reusable, loosely coupled code modules. The canonical preference is related but weaker than ensuring these properties; keep the outcome and evidence explicit.
Promote design patterns supporting modularity. Generic justified complexity does not establish modular-pattern adoption or promotion.

Verify inter-module dependencies are well documented. The canonical dependency-contract objective supports documentation, while this target specifically requires assessment of module dependency completeness.

Review technology-stack consistency across projects for efficiency and interoperability. Supported versions and reproducibility do not establish cross-project consistency or interoperability assessment.

Ensure technology-stack standardization to reduce complexity. Local justification and exceptions are legitimate decisions, but shared conventions do not automatically establish the source standardization outcome.
Verify chosen technologies are well supported and have a strong community. Supported version lists do not establish maintenance support or community health.
Check version control use for technology-stack dependencies. A generic configuration-change process does not establish versioned dependency-management configuration.
Ensure ephemeral resources can be recreated on demand. Reproducible environments support this, but preserve all relevant ephemeral resource classes and on-demand availability.
Ensure non-ephemeral compute has headroom for growth and scale. Monitoring resource use does not demonstrate sufficient persistent compute capacity.

Implement a load balancer routing traffic to appropriate resources. Generic load-distribution capability is not the explicit load-balancer recommendation; any justified alternative needs an explicit local decision.
Verify increased load can be handled without performance degradation. Define baseline and load regime explicitly; measuring bottlenecks alone cannot establish this outcome.
Check scalable storage use. Capacity planning alone does not establish use of scalable storage solutions.
Test disaster-recovery procedures regularly for actual operation. Generic tested backup restoration does not exhaust disaster recovery or its recurrence.
Document and review recovery-test results. Merely retaining restoration outcomes does not establish review of them.

Address issues identified during recovery testing. Test completion does not establish defect treatment; retain tracked unresolved defects instead of declaring recovery successful from execution alone.

Implement data-replication strategies to avoid data loss during disaster. Evaluation of replication is not implementation; record the source recommendation and any target-specific alternative or limit explicitly.
Verify replication processes are monitored. Replication existence does not establish process monitoring and monitoring evidence.
Ensure replicated data is consistent and current. A performed check does not establish the data-quality outcome if it fails; retain both observed results and unresolved gaps.

Ensure modular application services can be developed, deployed and scaled independently. Function-owned repositories and independent change ownership are related but do not establish service scaling or deployability.
Verify clear and well-defined module interfaces. Dependency/interface contracts support this, but stable documentation alone does not establish interface clarity.
Assess codebase modularity for easier updates and maintenance. Keep code-level modularity separate from repository structure and service topology.
Ensure reusable and loosely coupled code modules. This repeats source line192 under a different subsection; do not assert DUPLICATE until scope and source-level review establish equivalence.
Check use of design patterns promoting modularity. Keep the actual design-pattern assessment separate from the broad complexity objective.
Verify module dependencies are well documented. This resembles line194, but retain both occurrences until independent scope-aware deduplication is performed.
Consider microservices where appropriate. This is an evaluation, not a universal microservice mandate; preserve the suitability condition and record the decision.
Verify microservices are independently deployable when that architecture applies. Justifying services does not establish their actual independent deployment capability.
Ensure microservices communicate effectively. An interface document alone is not evidence of effective communication; scope this to selected microservices.

Check use of service discovery mechanisms within the microservices subsection. Scope may depend on architecture, but do not silently erase the check by declaring discovery unnecessary without a decision.
Assess need for custom integrations and ensure secure, efficient implementation. Integration ownership/contracts support governance but do not establish secure and efficient actual implementation.
Verify custom integrations are documented and maintained. Documentation maintenance alone does not establish maintenance of the integrations themselves.
Ensure custom integrations do not introduce security vulnerabilities. Risk review is supporting evidence and must not substitute for the stated safety outcome.
Ensure network configuration is optimized for security and performance. A review against requirements is evidence, not proof that appropriate configuration outcomes are achieved.
Verify firewalls and security groups are configured properly. Preserve both mechanisms and actual configuration assessment without inventing a universal rule set.
Ensure network traffic is monitored and analyzed for potential threats. Monitoring alone does not establish threat analysis; retain coverage and analysis evidence.
Apply patches and updates regularly for security and performance. General maintenance or available update configuration does not establish recurring application of both patches and updates.
Schedule maintenance windows and communicate them to stakeholders. Coordination alone does not establish scheduled windows and communication coverage.
Verify update procedures are documented and tested. Generic configuration rollback or policy change controls do not establish update-procedure documentation and testing.
Plan hardware scaling for future growth. Resource monitoring supports planning but does not establish a documented hardware scaling strategy.
Review and update capacity planning regularly. Monitoring performance is supporting evidence rather than proof of recurring plan review and updates.
Check use of scalable infrastructure components. Planning for growth does not establish current component scalability or actual use.

Implement robust backup solutions tailored to on-premises deployment. Selecting a suitable mechanism does not establish implementation; generic recovery tests do not define all on-premises backup needs.
Verify documented and tested backup procedures. Preserve verification of procedures, documentation and tests as distinct from a successful restoration example.
Ensure secure backup storage and quick restoration. Restoration objectives should define quick for the target, but an unspecified acceptable time cannot silently weaken the source goal.
Ensure simple, understandable codebases. Justified architectural complexity supports this, but code-level comprehensibility needs its own evidence.
Verify code follows best practices and coding standards. Adopted local guidance must be explicit; it cannot be assumed to exhaust the upstream recommendation without review.
Check code-review use to maintain code quality. Reviewer threshold and staffing choices do not establish actual code-quality review or its content.
Ensure code is well documented. Onboarding and working examples support usage but do not establish adequate code documentation.
Design systems as simply as possible while meeting requirements. Preserve the requirements constraint and actual simplification goal; a stated preference does not establish the design outcome.
Verify system architecture is straightforward and easy to understand. Justified complexity is related but does not demonstrate clarity and comprehension.
Ensure system configuration is straightforward and easy to manage. Understandability alone does not establish operational manageability.
Check design-pattern use that promotes simplicity. Complexity justification alone does not establish this specific design-pattern assessment.
Maintain clear, concise documentation for all systems and processes. Reproducible onboarding docs do not establish the full system/process denominator.
Verify documentation is current and accessible. Revision correlation supports currency, but access by the intended audience remains a separate requirement.
Ensure documentation includes examples and use cases. Working usage examples support the objective, but use cases must remain explicit rather than only general usage context.
Check use of documentation tools for managing and publishing documentation. This is a capability assessment, not a mandate for a particular product or public distribution.

Implement comprehensive logging of system behavior and issues. Actionable logs support the objective but need explicit coverage; recording selected relevant behavior cannot silently replace comprehensiveness.
Verify logs are securely stored and available for analysis. Controlled access and sensitive-data handling support this, while actual storage security and analyst access need evidence.
Ensure log-retention policies are in place. Approved retention supports this; defining a requirement alone does not establish an operative policy.
Check use of log-aggregation tools. A target may justify an alternative, but an evaluation of appropriateness cannot erase assessment of current tool use.
